title: How Sensitive Are Your Eyes?
hook: What is the faintest thing a human eye can possibly see?
script: What is the faintest thing a human eye can possibly see? Most people think our vision is surprisingly weak in the dark. In reality, your eyes can register one particle of light. Each retina packs 120 million rod cells designed to trap a single photon. When hit, a molecule inside flips in less than a trillionth of a second. That tiny packet carries so little energy it cannot lift a grain of sand. Yet on a dark clear night, your eyes can catch a candle flame miles away. You are sensing light at the smallest amount possible in physics.
